Incorporating the April 2018 SLOOS, the macro tone of the FOMC statement remains positive—strong growth, low unemployment, inflation near 2%, and balanced risks—but credit conditions show a few mild headwinds. Banks reported widened loan rate spreads, credit policies for commercial real estate changed, and CRE loan demand shifted, while standards for qualified jumbo mortgages were unchanged and banks continued to extend credit to customers. This mix suggests slightly tighter financial conditions at the margin, which could modestly temper the otherwise pro-growth backdrop. Net: still positive and accommodative, but a touch less upbeat than a macro-only read.
